reason: page.webmcp.tools() lists the tools a page or frame registers. Strider has no WebMCP discovery API, and reading the page's own registrations would test the script rather than Strider
page.webmcp.callTool(name, input) calls a registered tool and returns its result, or throws the error the browser reports. Strider has no WebMCP tool-call API

callTool's timeout option, which bounds a tool that does not settle (WM-007) or a declarative tool waiting for a submit (WM-011), and whose Timeout error names the bound. Strider has no WebMCP tool-call API to take it
A frame's own webmcp property, which lists and calls the tools its frame registers. Strider's frames have no WebMCP operation, though `page.frame(locator)` can enter a frame
